To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the normalized quadratic reciprocal function is the best of the five forms, (2) all of the five forms are inferior to the generalized Leontief form, (3) the Minflex Laurent form performs the worst, (4) all five forms violate the curvature conditions, and (5) the curvature conditions are maintained by the generalized Leontieff and normalized quadratic forms, while the basic translog and the almost ideal demand forms do not maintain the curvature conditions.

the Minflex Laurent and the normalized quadratic are the best functional forms, that the basic translog and the generalized Leontief are not very far behind, and that the almost ideal demand function system is the worst.

the Minflex Laurent and the normalized quadratic recursive indirect utility function are the most flexible of the functional forms, and that both satisfy the theoretical conditions of monotonicity and curvature, while the other three functional forms violate one or more of these regularity conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical and policy implications of the curvature property of functional forms in applied econometrics, with an emphasis on the demand for assets.
the empirical performance of these five flexible functional forms in the context of the demand for assets.
the specification of a flexible functional form for the demand for money and the estimation of a full set (including the own-price elasticity) of the associated elasticities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Minflex Laurent is a clear winner in the sense of satisfying the regularity conditions of economic theory.

the almost ideal demand function, with the curvature condition, is the best of the five functional forms, in terms of the regularity and curvature properties, and in terms of the full set of price and income elasticities.
the Minflex Laurent is the best of a very bad bunch.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the almost ideal demand systems are the preferred functional form, and that the normalized quadratic reciprocal function is also a strong candidate.
the Minflex Laurent form is a very good approximation to the data and that, in the context of a demand system, the generalized Leontief is a poor approximation.
there is no one functional form that is clearly superior to the others, in terms of the theoretical regularity properties, and the output in terms of elasticities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the demand for money is not a single entity, but a collection of demand functions for individual money types.
the Minflex Laurent and the normalized quadratic are the best functional forms in terms of the regularity and output measures.

the choice of functional form is a critical issue in the analysis of consumer demand and that the choice of form is not a matter of taste or convenience, but rather of the theoretical regularity that is maintained.
